plant.culled_by: TWO INDEPENDENT EYES. Rafe, device walk, 2026-09-06; and round 30's blind seat, 2026-09-06.
plant.verbatim: flat pale block, no interior texture (seat) / too shiny on worn areas, character washed out (Rafe)

seat.BEST_WHY: The wall course at y≈390–450, running from x=180 to the corridor mouth at x=500. It is two stacked runs of stone with vertical timbers driven through them at x≈270, 348, 415, 480 — and the courses do not line up. The upper run's block breaks fall at different intervals from the lower run's, the timber at x≈348 crosses both courses while the one at x≈415 only crosses the upper, and one block at x≈425 has a small L-shaped patch let into its face at a different value from the surrounding stone. That is a wall someone built out of what was to hand and then pinned, rather than a repeated tile. Second thing, at the corridor mouth x≈500–520, y≈380–460: the timber ends there are cut short and the stone beside them is chewed back, so the corridor edge reads as a hole that was widened and then braced, not as a gap left in a tileset. Third: in the lit pool immediately left of the figure, x≈230–390, y≈460–560, the flagstone joints are legible as a grid but the joint *width* changes along a single run — the horizontal joint at y≈505 is 1px from x=230 to x=290 and 2px from x=300 to x=370. The stones read as cut and settled.
seat.WORST_WHY: Two incompatible projections in one 384×288 frame, roughly 100px apart. The crates at x≈64–97, y≈0–90 are drawn in **elevation** — you are looking at their front faces, you can count vertical plank lines running down the lower half of each, and each casts a soft drop shadow downward onto the dirt as if lit from behind the camera. The barrels at x≈112–135 and x≈160–183, y≈188–215 are drawn as top ellipse **plus staved body receding downward**, so their height occupies vertical screen space, and they cast no shadow at all. The flagstone floor beneath them is flat top-down. Worse, both barrels' bodies are **sliced flat by the dirt/flagstone seam at y≈215** — the staves just stop on a dead horizontal line at a floor-material boundary. An object clipped by a texture edge is the single most placeholder-looking thing in the deck. On top of that the frame has **no light falloff whatsoever**: the premise is a figure carrying the only light there is, and this image is at identical exposure from x=0 to x=383. And the brick at x≈165–186, y≈272–278 in the bottom course is a visibly lighter grey than every other brick in that run — one wrong tile, sitting in the middle of the frame's bottom edge.
seat.FLAGGED:
2, 4, 1, 3

- **2** — the barrel/crate projection clash and the sliced barrel bases, above.
- **4** — a diagonal streak overlay across the entire lit pool, x≈340–520, y≈450–600, running lower-left to upper-right at a constant angle with constant spacing. It crosses stone and joint indiscriminately and, critically, it *erases* the flagstone joint grid that 1 and 3 both have in that exact area: in 1 you can count five individual flagstones left of the figure, in 4 that same area is one smeared bright wash. This is the literal "a filter was run over it" failure, and the pixel-diff confirms it is the only meaningful difference between 1 and 4.
- **1 and 3 share one flag**: a dead-straight vertical material seam at x≈380–440, running from y≈460 to the bottom edge. Left of it: large square flagstones on a ~40px grid, cool grey-green cast. Right of it: small running-bond bricks, roughly 48×22, warm tan. Two floor materials at two different stone scales butted edge to edge with no threshold course, no jamb, no wear transition. You see it at a glance because the value and hue both jump on the same line. (4 has this too; it is flagged above for the worse fault.)

flip_list: Everything in FLIP 1 applies — 3 carries the same material seam, the same unlit-rectangle hard edges, the same lighting-independent crack, and the same repeated hatch stamp.

The band at x≈180–500, y≈385–430, directly above the pin course, is structureless soft brown mottle — no block breaks, no joints, no edges — while the identical region in 1 is articulated stone. Rebuild that band with the same block-and-timber language as the course below it, or cut the wall thinner so the mottle isn't there.
The transition from that mottle into the pin course at y≈430 is a soft blur. Put a hard 1px edge on the top of the pin course so the two read as different surfaces rather than one gradient.
law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
